name: Rahab
summary: A woman of Jericho described as a harlot who hides Joshua's two spies on her roof, misleads the king's men, and lets the spies down by a cord from her window. She tells them that fear of Israel has fallen on the land and asks for kindness to her father's household in return. When Jericho falls she and her family are spared, and she lives among Israel. The New Testament names her in Matthew's genealogy and cites her in Hebrews and James.

residence: A house on the town wall of Jericho (Joshua 2:15)

name: Achan
summary: A man of Judah who takes some of the devoted spoil from Jericho, a Babylonish garment, silver and a wedge of gold, and hides it in his tent. Israel then loses at Ai. When lots single him out he confesses that he coveted the goods and took them. Israel stones him and burns the goods, and the place is named the valley of Achor.

residence: Israel's camp at Jericho and Ai (Joshua 7:1)
Valley of Achor, where he is buried under stones (Joshua 7:26)

name: Othniel
summary: Kenaz's son and a younger brother of Caleb. He captures a town and receives Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife. When Israel cries out under Chushanrishathaim of Mesopotamia, the Lord raises him as deliverer, the Spirit of the Lord comes on him, and the land has rest forty years until he dies.

geography.origin: Not stated beyond his family of Kenaz (Judges 3:9)

name: Ehud
summary: A left-handed Benjamite, son of Gera, whom the Lord raises up when Israel cries out under Eglon king of Moab. He brings Eglon the tribute, then returns to kill him with a dagger and escapes. He rallies Israel, Moab is subdued, and the land has rest eighty years.

name: Deborah
summary: A prophetess and the wife of Lapidoth who judges Israel from beneath a palm tree in the hill country of Ephraim. She summons Barak to lead ten thousand men against Sisera, agrees to go with him, and says the Lord will sell Sisera into a woman's hand. She is the speaker or subject of the song in Judges 5 after the victory.

geography.origin: Not stated; she held court in the hill country of Ephraim (Judges 4:5)
residence: Under the palm tree of Deborah, between Ramah and Bethel (Judges 4:5)

name: Barak
summary: Abinoam's son from Kedesh-naphtali, summoned by Deborah to gather ten thousand men at Mount Tabor against Sisera. He insists that she go with him, and she warns that the honour of the victory will pass to a woman. He pursues Sisera and finds him dead in Jael's tent. Hebrews 11 names him among those commended for faith.

residence: Mount Tabor, where he musters the army (Judges 4:6)

name: Jael
summary: The wife of Heber the Kenite, whose tent Sisera flees to after his army is routed, since there was peace between Jabin and Heber's house. She welcomes him, and while he sleeps she drives a tent nail through his temples. She shows Barak the dead man, and Deborah's song blesses her above women in the tent.

name: Gideon
summary: Joash's son, an Abiezrite from the tribe of Manasseh, threshing wheat in a winepress when the angel of the Lord appears and calls him to save Israel from Midian. He asks for the fleece sign, reduces his army to three hundred, and routs Midian with trumpets and torches in jars. He declines to rule, but makes an ephod that becomes a snare to Israel and his house.

children: Abimelech, by a concubine at Shechem

name: Abimelech
summary: Gideon's son by a concubine from Shechem. With the backing of his mother's kin he kills his seventy brothers on one stone, leaving only Jotham, and is made king at Shechem. After God sends an evil spirit between him and Shechem's men he destroys the city, and a woman breaks his skull with a millstone at Thebez. The text says God repaid his wickedness.

name: Jephthah
summary: A Gileadite warrior, son of Gilead and a harlot, whom the elders recall to lead against Ammon. The Spirit of the Lord comes on him and he vows that whatever first comes from his house to meet him will be the Lord's and offered as a burnt offering. His only child, his daughter, comes out first, and the text says he did with her according to his vow. He later fights Ephraim at the Jordan fords. He judges Israel six years.

name: Samson
summary: Son of Manoah of the Danites, announced as a Nazarite from the womb who would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines. He marries a Philistine woman of Timnath, kills many Philistines, and judges Israel twenty years. Delilah learns that his strength lies in his uncut hair; he is shaved, blinded and made to grind in Gaza's prison. At the Philistine temple he asks to die with them and brings the house down.

geography.origin: Zorah, of the family of the Danites (Judges 13:2)

name: Delilah
summary: A woman Samson loves in the valley of Sorek. The lords of the Philistines tell her to entice him to reveal the source of his great strength, and she presses him until he tells her. She has him sleep on her knees and calls for a man to shave his seven locks, after which his strength leaves him.

name: Naomi
summary: The wife of Elimelech, an Ephrathite of Bethlehem, who goes to Moab in a famine and there loses her husband and her sons Mahlon and Chilion. She returns to Bethlehem with her daughter-in-law Ruth and asks to be called Mara, saying the Almighty has dealt bitterly with her. She guides Ruth toward Boaz, and when Obed is born the neighbour women say a son is born to Naomi.

linked_stories.title: Naomi and Ruth Return to Bethlehem

name: Ruth
summary: A Moabite woman who marries Mahlon, Naomi's son, and after his death refuses to leave Naomi, saying her people and God shall be hers. In Bethlehem she gleans in the field of Boaz, a kinsman, and on Naomi's advice asks him at the threshing floor to act as near kinsman. He marries her, and she bears Obed, the father of Jesse and grandfather of David. Matthew's genealogy names her.

linked_stories.title: Naomi and Ruth Return to Bethlehem

name: Boaz
summary: A wealthy kinsman of Elimelech's family in Bethlehem who lets Ruth glean in his field. When she asks him at the threshing floor to spread his skirt over her as near kinsman, he arranges the redemption at the gate, buys the inheritance, and takes Ruth as his wife to raise up the dead man's name. Their son Obed is the father of Jesse. Matthew lists him as Booz, son of Salmon and Rachab.
